verdicts.critique: P1 is the only proposal that clears the gating condition (an expected-return component not proportional to the covariance loadings), and I cannot refute that necessity. But the mechanism as specified hands most of the new premium to FM, not DKKM, and the proposal's own evidence says so. The wedge is discoverable ONLY because it contaminates the characteristics: log bm_obs = log bm_fund + q, size_obs = size_fund - q. So the numerator of the new alpha, alpha_i = (1-rho)*q_it, is by construction an ADDITIVE component of two raw characteristics. FM's weight is w_i,t = a_t'x_it + b (fama_functions.py:158-165, P = X pinvh(X'X) refit every month), so a linear read of bm_obs and size_obs recovers q up to the fundamental-bm confound. That is exactly the proposer's own span2.py cell 'linear alpha, homogeneous d', where RFF/lin = 1.00 -- ZERO DKKM advantage. P1 alone therefore raises SR* a lot and moves the DKKM/FM ratio by nothing. The DKKM-specific content is only (i) the 1/(d_f + kappa^2 sigma_v^2) denominator and (ii) the kappa-hump. On (i), the proposer's own est3.py numbers for 'linear alpha + het d' are lin 0.265, QUAD(21) 0.601, RFF(3600) 0.564 -- a 21-term quadratic OLS BEATS the 3600-feature ridge. That is a virtue of one interaction layer, not a virtue of complexity, and it is available to FM at the cost of appending 15 cross-product columns. On (ii), the hump requires s_k ~ 1.9, which the proposer concedes makes E[kappa^2] = kappa_med^2 * exp(2*1.9^2) = 1370x kappa_med^2: with N=1000 and a lognormal that heavy, SR*^2 = sum_i alpha_i^2/d_i is dominated by the top handful of firms. That is precisely the corruption failure mode -- max_sr becomes a 5-firm artifact, the true w* concentrates on those firms, and cos_Sigma(w_hat, w*) falls for EVERY method including DKKM. Separately, the fork between 'log kappa ~ N permanent firm attribute' and 'kappa = g(mve, sigma_idio)' is decisive and unresolved: the permanent-random version is not a function of the characteristics at all, so it is unlearnable noise for all three estimators and only inflates the denominator of Sharpe/SR*. Only the char-deterministic version can help, and that version makes kappa an exponential of a linear function of two chars -- a smooth two-dimensional surface, i.e. the low-order regime where the audit already measured the RFF basis to be 88% cubic.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM CAN capture it: alpha_i = (1-rho)*kappa_i*v_it = (1-rho)*q_it, and q_it enters log bm_obs and size_obs ADDITIVELY, so the premium is linear in two contaminated characteristics and FM's monthly X(X'X)^{-1} span contains it exactly. FF CAN capture much of it: hml is a tercile long-short in bm_obs, which is monotone in q, and because FF value-weights within buckets (fama_functions.py:88-99, weights proportional to mve within (high & big) etc.), the FF factor set is literally {size x step-function-of-char}, so the leading size-modulation of kappa is a two-bin FF interaction. THE GAP IS SECOND-ORDER: taking the proposal's own calibration, SR_alpha = 0.6/month of which the linear-in-chars part is fully FM-spanned; the residual DKKM-only part is the ratio curvature, which span2.py prices at RFF/lin = 1.91 in POPULATION and est3.py prices at RFF(3600) 0.564 vs QUAD(21) 0.601 with estimation noise -- i.e. DKKM LOSES to a 21-term quadratic. Converting: on BGN's current scale that is FM ~0.30, quadratic-FM ~0.35, DKKM ~0.33 per month. A ratio of 1.1x, not 3-5x. NOISE-FASTER-THAN-SIGNAL: the wedge adds kappa_i^2*sigma_v^2 to every diagonal, i.e. it adds pure idiosyncratic variance to all 1000 firms while adding exploitable alpha to only the tail of the kappa distribution; at s_k = 1.9 the median firm gets almost all noise and almost no signal, which is the regime where ridge-on-3600 features loses to a 6-parameter fit. METRIC: the population conditional Sharpe CAN detect this (it is SR* x cos_Sigma), but HJD as currently coded cannot, because raising SR* from 0.30 to 0.64/month drives sd(sdf_ret) down and E[sdf_ret] up, compressing the whole HJD range (the audit's table: at SR*=2 the entire span from rho=0 to rho=1 is 13% of the level).
verdicts.salvage: Keep the wedge, but change three things so the premium is NOT linear in any characteristic. (1) Make kappa depend on a THREE-WAY interaction that FF's 2x3 design cannot form and that is not size-monotone: e.g. kappa_i = f(idio-vol percentile) x g(turnover/age) x h(|bm - cross-sectional median|), with h non-monotone. (2) Make the demand shock v_it enter the observables only through a NON-MONOTONE or ratio channel, so that no single contaminated char is an affine read of q -- e.g. let v drive a temporary component of BOTH price and reported book so that q is identified only by the DIFFERENCE of two chars divided by a third. (3) Before running any estimator, compute the population gate: mean_t sqrt(rp' S (S'Sigma S)^{-1} S' rp) / sqrt(rp' X (X'Sigma X)^{-1} X' rp) with X = [1, chars, all 15 quadratic cross-products] in the denominator, not just linear chars. If that ratio is below ~2 against the QUADRATIC benchmark, the wedge has not created complexity, only nonlinearity, and the paper's claim must be re-scoped. Also cap s_k at the value where the top 10 firms contribute less than 25% of SR*^2, and report that share in every table.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2. Estimator geometry repair (bandwidth, second rank-standardization, NMAT, alpha grid, c=P/T)
verdicts.critique: The diagnosis is largely right and the proposal admits its own standalone value is approximately zero. Beyond that, three items are wrong or counterproductive. (a) THE EXACT CHANGE FOR THE ALPHA GRID TARGETS DEAD CODE. P2(d) says to reparameterize 'utils_factors/dkkm_functions.py lines 162 and 176 from 360*z to 360*z*trace(X'X)/P'. But mve_data calls ridge_regr with shrinkage_list = np.array([0]) at BOTH line 301 (the alpha=0 column) and line 314 (every alpha>0 column). The penalty for alpha>0 is delivered entirely by the augmentation matrix np.sqrt(360*alph)*np.eye(X.shape[1])[:-1] at line 309. So the proposed edit changes nothing for any nonzero alpha and only touches the already-degenerate alpha=0 path. The correct site is line 309. This matters because the whole proposal is sold as 'derived, not tuned' and the derivation would be applied at a location where it has no effect. (b) NMAT=1 MAKES DKKM WORSE IN LEVEL. Averaging 5 independent W draws is a variance reduction on the estimated stock weight (estimate_sdf_dkkm.py:134-169 accumulates sw_i = fw_i @ pof_i and divides by NMAT). The theoretical argument that this converges to kernel ridge and flattens the complexity CURVE is correct, but the goal here is a large DKKM Sharpe ADVANTAGE, and removing a 5x variance reduction will lower DKKM's realized Sharpe. P2 is trading level for curve shape and does not say so. (c) THE FAIRNESS FIX IS SELF-DEFEATING FOR THE STATED GOAL. P2(f) gives FF/FM the same ridge grid and the same post-hoc alpha selection. Ridge on a 7-factor plug-in tangency at T=360 is worth roughly the 2K/T = 3.9% squared-Sharpe loss, so FF/FM go UP and the gap goes DOWN. Correct science, but it should be labelled as shrinking the target, not enabling it. (d) The gamma rescale is measured to HURT on the current DGPs (GS21: 0.879 -> 0.799 of max SR^2 at gamma x4.65 with 36 features; 0.879 -> 0.376 at x10), and P3, which P2 leans on to justify it, does not actually deliver sd(Wx) = gamma*sqrt(35/12) once the chars are collinear (see my P3 critique).
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: By the proposal's own admission the gap produced is zero on the current models, and the audit bounds it at 0.7pp of Sharpe in BGN and +3% in GS21. Conditional on P1/P4, FM captures the same thing because none of P2 changes what is in the DGP -- it only changes how well DKKM can reach a nonlinearity that must be created elsewhere, and if that nonlinearity turns out to be quadratic (the est3.py evidence), then P2's contribution is negative: it spends the feature budget on high-frequency directions that a 21-term quadratic already covers, which is exactly the measured GS21 result. NOISE FASTER THAN SIGNAL is the central risk here and it is measured, not speculative: widening gamma raises effective rank from 16.5 to 78 but the added directions carry no signal under any low-order truth, so ridge must shrink harder and the realized Sharpe falls (est3.py: linear alpha + hom d gives RFF3600 0.254 vs RFFx8 0.157, a 38% loss). METRIC: P=36000 at c=100 will also re-create alpha=0 pathologies unless the alpha=0 column is removed; note line 301 unconditionally emits it regardless of the grid.
verdicts.salvage: Do three of the five, at the right code sites, and drop the other two. KEEP: (i) the alpha grid, implemented at dkkm_functions.py:309 as sqrt(360*alph*trace(X'X)/P) so z is a scale-free shrinkage fraction, and delete the unconditional alpha=0 column at line 301 (or truncate small eigenvalues in the P>=T branch at line 176); (ii) the second-rank-standardization -> per-column z-score at line 110, which is the one change that both restores gamma-dependence and preserves the amplitude equalization the audit measured to be load-bearing; (iii) the fairness repairs (same grid for FF/FM, drop the BGN-only rf_stand at lines 95-96, turn on the FM standardization at fama_functions.py:152-156) -- do these unconditionally, as correctness. DROP: NMAT=1 (keep 5 and report the cross-draw spread separately as a robustness panel), and the gamma rescale (make it a reported 2x2 robustness cell, never the headline). Add one thing P2 omits: a QUADRATIC-OLS benchmark column (FM plus all 15 cross-products, ridge-tuned on the same grid). If DKKM cannot beat that, there is no virtue of complexity to report regardless of what the bandwidth does.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3. Expand the characteristic set from 5-6 to ~35 model-generated signals
verdicts.critique: The load-bearing quantitative claim is wrong. P3 asserts EffRank ~ 16.5*(L/5)^1.42 -> ~250 at L=35, citing the measured grid L=5 -> 16.5, L=20 -> 98, L=130 -> 773. That grid was measured with characteristics that are (near-)independent draws. The eigenvalue decay of a Gaussian-kernel feature map is governed by the INTRINSIC dimension of the data manifold, not the ambient column count: features are sin(gamma*g'x), and if x lies on a 3-dimensional manifold then every feature is a function of 3 coordinates and the RKHS is the 3-dimensional Gaussian RKHS no matter how many collinear coordinates you stack. The audit already established the intrinsic dimension: BGN's entire date-t cross-section is a bijective function of exactly two numbers, (num_i, sum_j exp(-beta_j)) <-> (book_i, mve_i), verified to machine precision; GS21's state is (k, b, z) with bm = 1/P_ex EXACTLY; KP14's chars recover nlive and log d at R^2 0.82-0.88 and nothing else. P3's 35 columns -- five momentum horizons, four asset-growth horizons, five profitability transforms, four valuation anchors, five risk measures, three scale measures, four lags -- are all deterministic smooth transforms of those same 2-3 states plus a common aggregate. Effective rank will move from 16.5 to maybe 25-40, not 250. Note the arithmetic P3 itself supplies and then ignores: sd(Wx) = gamma*sqrt(L/12) is derived assuming Var(w'x) = sum_i g_i^2/12, i.e. UNCORRELATED chars; with 35 chars whose correlation matrix has effective rank 3, E_g[g'Sigma_x g] = tr(Sigma_x) is unchanged but the feature map's SPECTRUM collapses -- the quantity that matters for DKKM Theorem 3 is the spectrum, not the index sd. Second problem: P3 concedes that the honest DKKM-vs-FM channel at L=35 is FM's 2K/T = 20.6% squared-Sharpe estimation cost. That is manufacturing a gap by degrading the benchmark, and it is worse for FF, which gets 35 collinear tercile long-shorts fed into an unpenalized OLS tangency (fama_functions.mve_data uses sklearn Ridge with alpha=0). Third problem: P3's own risk section notes that several derived chars will be >20% ties (agr is already 91% zeros in BGN, 98.8% in GS21), and the audit measured that a tied column becomes a persistent pseudo-random characteristic that enters ALL 3600 features multiplicatively, raising the PCs needed for 99% of feature variance from 59 to 95. Adding 35 columns of which several are degenerate injects noise into DKKM's basis multiplicatively while injecting it into FM's design additively -- the asymmetry runs AGAINST DKKM.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM CAN capture whatever new information exists, because 35 smooth transforms of a 3-dimensional state contain no information the original 5 did not, and FM spans every linear combination of all 35. FF's degradation is real but is benchmark sabotage, not complexity. THE ARITHMETIC: the audit's own headroom numbers cap the total nonlinearity available in BGN at 0.7 percentage points of Sharpe (deg-3 poly 0.2761 vs FM 0.2740 out of max 0.2985) and in GS21 at +3%. Those ceilings are properties of the DGP and are INVARIANT to how many transforms of the same state you hand the econometrician -- the population span calculation uses rp and cond_var, not chars. So P3 cannot move the ceiling by a single basis point; it can only move where each estimator sits relative to it, and it moves FM and FF DOWN. Expect a DKKM/FM ratio of 1.2-1.3x that is pure estimation efficiency, which P3 admits. ADDS NOISE FASTER THAN SIGNAL: yes, and measurably -- degenerate tie columns multiply into every feature.
verdicts.salvage: One piece survives and should be extracted as its own proposal: the 'peer-relative' block (viii), which requires a firm-type / industry partition. A fixed partition into 10 groups correlated with the model's PERMANENT firm heterogeneity (beta_j in BGN, lambda_f in KP14, initial k in GS21) is the only element of P3 that adds a genuinely new state dimension rather than a transform of an existing one. But even that is captured by FM the moment you give FM the industry dummies, so it must be paired with type-DEPENDENT nonlinear pricing, not just type demeaning. Everything else in P3 should be dropped, and if a wider characteristic set is wanted for realism, cap it at L ~ 12 and pre-screen every column on (a) tie fraction < 10% and (b) partial R^2 above 2% against the existing set, and publish the measured EffRank of the resulting feature map rather than the extrapolated one.

verdicts.proposal_name: P4. Recalibrate the idiosyncratic-risk block (level, dispersion, char-nonlinearity)
verdicts.critique: The realism case is unanswerable -- pairwise correlations of 0.565 (BGN), 0.391 (KP14) and 0.95 (GS21) against a real-data 0.15-0.20 are indefensible and should be fixed regardless. But as a route to a DKKM advantage it fails on my central test, and the proposal's own numbers say so: standalone it is worth 0.19% of SR* at N=1000 and it LOWERS max_sr in all three models. The multiplier argument then rests on w* = alpha(x)/d(x) being unreachable by the benchmarks, and that is where it breaks. In every one of the three models the measured d is a MONOTONE function of size: KP14 has corr(log idio var, log nlive) = -0.971 with slope -0.866 and corr(log idio var, log mve) giving R^2 0.743; BGN has corr(log d, log(bm/mve)) = 0.910; GS21 has R^2 of diag(Sigma) on linear chars of 0.68-0.84. So w* ~ alpha(x) * size^theta -- a product of a characteristic signal and a power of size. That is EXACTLY what a value-weighted 2x3 double sort forms. Reading fama_functions.py:88-104: high_big = mve*(high & big) normalized within bucket, and factor = 0.5*(high_big + high_small - low_big - low_small), so the FF factor's weight on firm i is proportional to mve_i times a step function of the sort char. A tangency combination over {smb, hml, cma, rmw, umd, mkt} therefore spans a family of size-weighted step functions in each characteristic -- a coarse but genuine product basis in exactly the (size x char) direction that P4's het-d channel creates. P4's own caveat says 'if d is a MONOTONE function of a single characteristic, FF's tercile sorts get a crude approximation', and then it does not act on that caveat: the proposed recalibrations (removing BGN's 0.1 factor, restoring KP14's sigmas, raising GS21 sigma_z) all produce size-monotone dispersion. The only non-monotone version offered is 'ride on P1's wedge', which makes P4 a rider on a proposal that itself needs fixing. Second problem: KP14's idio-var-proportional-to-1/size structure is what produces the documented anti-size artifact and the negative Sharpes; raising sigma_eps/sigma_u restores the CIR share to 69% and breaks that identity, which is a genuine bug fix, but it is a SIGN fix, not a complexity gain, and it should be reported as such rather than as evidence for the paper's thesis.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FF CAN capture the leading term, for the specific reason above: value-weighting inside a size-split double sort IS an estimator of a size x char product, and the audit measures d to be size-monotone in all three models. FM captures the alpha numerator. THE ARITHMETIC, standalone: the inverse-variance tilt under exact factor pricing is worth 1/(2*sigma_f^2*beta'D^{-1}beta), measured at 0.186% of SR* at N=1000 -- roughly 0.0006 of monthly Sharpe on BGN's 0.2985 max. That is sub-basis-point and undetectable. Conditional on P1, the span2.py multiplier takes RFF/lin from 1.00 to 1.91, but that same cell in est3.py with T=360 noise gives QUAD(21) 0.601 > RFF(3600) 0.564, so once estimation error is included the ratio-nonlinearity is captured by a quadratic and DKKM does not win. CORRUPTION RISK, which is the failure mode I was asked to check and it is live here: raising GS21_SIGMA_Z from 0.1x to 0.5x makes default a live event for the first time (currently 0 defaults in 2,163,000 firm-months, z_cut_down pinned at the grid floor everywhere), and the arbitrary floor P_ex = max(0.05/k, P_ex) at panel_functions_gs21.py:131 then produces near-zero prices, enormous bm, tiny d and near-singular cond_var passed to np.linalg.solve, which raises no error. This is not hypothetical -- the original-vol run already produced true SDF weights up to 1e9. A handful of near-default firms would then carry all of max_sr, every method's cos_Sigma would collapse, and both metrics would be garbage. METRIC: raising idio vol lowers SR* everywhere, so all reported Sharpes fall and the paper's headline numbers get smaller even if the ratio improves.
verdicts.salvage: Split it. (1) Do the realism recalibration unconditionally as a correctness fix, headline it as 'the models were mis-calibrated by 10x on idiosyncratic risk', and report the resulting max_sr, pairwise correlation and sd(log d) against real-data targets. Fix KP14's quadrature (integ_kp14.py:43) and stale G_func.csv FIRST; nothing in KP14 is interpretable until then. (2) For GS21, add a hard guard before any re-solve: assert min eigenvalue of cond_var above a threshold, remove the P_ex floor at panel_functions_gs21.py:131 rather than relying on it, and report the top-10-firm share of SR*^2 every month. (3) If the het-d channel is to carry any weight, the dispersion must be driven by a NON-MONOTONE or at least a two-characteristic INTERACTION -- e.g. idio variance that is U-shaped in bm within size groups -- so that a value-weighted 2x3 sort cannot approximate it. And in every table, report the quadratic-OLS benchmark next to DKKM; if a 21-term quadratic captures the ratio, the result is 'nonlinearity pays', which is a different and much weaker paper.

verdicts.proposal_name: P5. Metric repair (scale-free pricing error, Sharpe/max_sr, unconditional Sharpe, better test assets)
verdicts.critique: Items (b), (c) and (d) are unambiguously correct and cheap, and (b) in particular is the single most valuable line of code in all six proposals: evaluate_sdfs.py reads m['rp'], m['cond_var'] and m['sdf_ret'] at lines 170-172 but never m['max_sr'], so the ceiling never reaches a table and nobody can tell a failing estimator from an empty model. Item (a) is where I push back. The proposed replacement, sqrt(1 - rho_unc^2) with rho_unc the uncentered correlation, is in POPULATION a deterministic monotone transform of the quantity the Sharpe column already reports. Proof: sdf_ret is the projection of the constant 1 onto the full return span and xret_m is (approximately) the projection of 1 onto the method's span, so for any u in the span, E[u*z] = E[u], giving E[y*z] = E[y] = E[y^2] and E[z^2] = E[z]. Hence rho_unc^2 = E[y]/E[z] = [SR_m^2/(1+SR_m^2)] / [SR*^2/(1+SR*^2)], and 1 - rho_unc^2 is a strictly decreasing function of SR_m/SR* -- exactly the Sigma-cosine that P5(b) introduces. So the 'fixed' pricing-error column carries essentially no independent information; the paper would report the same number twice under two names. That is arguably worse than the current HJD, which at least has independent (if contaminated) content through the leverage and direction errors of the finite-sample weights. Second issue: P5(d) proposes test assets sorted on deciles of the TRUE conditional MVE weight w*_t = solve(cond_var, rp). Those are oracle-constructed test assets -- a referee will note that the test portfolios were built from the answer, and that any method whose weights correlate with w* will price them by construction. Third, minor but real: P5 correctly flags the universe mismatch at evaluate_sdfs.py:170-171 (rp and cond_var subset to firm_ids, sdf_ret computed over the book>0 universe) but files it as a footnote; in KP14 that is roughly 5% of firms per month with rp = -1.0 exactly, so it is not cosmetic.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: It cannot, and the proposal says so. Nothing here changes the DGP, the estimator or the span. What it can do is REVEAL that no gap exists: the Sigma-cosine column will show FF at roughly 0.81 of the ceiling in BGN and DKKM at 0.85, which settles the diagnosis in one line. The adversarial risk to be honest about is that P5 makes DKKM look WORSE on two dimensions simultaneously: a scale-free pricing error removes DKKM's current advantage of having six alphas post-hoc selected on the evaluation metric itself (create_slides_tables.find_best_alpha_for_model), while FF/FM get only alpha=0; and the unconditional Sharpe will penalize methods whose monthly leverage is erratic, which at nfeatures=3600, alpha=0 is DKKM (mve_data line 301 always emits the min-norm interpolating column).
verdicts.salvage: Do (b), (c) and the universe fix immediately -- they are pure correctness and require no re-simulation if the moments pickles are retained. For (a), do NOT replace HJD with a monotone transform of Sharpe. Instead report the object compute_pricing_errors.py already computes -- alpha' Sigma^{-1} alpha with each method's MVE return as a single factor -- since that has genuinely independent content, and demote HJD to a robustness table with sd(sdf_ret) and the w=0 null printed alongside so readers can see the floor. For (d), keep the (mve, diag(cond_var)) 5x5 and ADD interaction-sorted and non-monotone-sorted assets (|bm - median| terciles crossed with size, roe x agr), which are constructible from observables; drop the true-w*-decile assets or relegate them to an explicitly labelled oracle diagnostic. Finally add the one column that would make all six proposals falsifiable: the population span ratio mean_t SR_rff,t / SR_quad,t computed from the true rp and cond_var, with a QUADRATIC (not linear) denominator.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6. Reporting lags with staggered fiscal year-ends plus heteroskedastic measurement error
verdicts.critique: The theoretical observation is correct and elegant -- classical homoskedastic EIV attenuates nonlinear Fourier components by exp(-omega^2 sigma_e^2/2) while attenuating the linear component only by tau^2/(tau^2+sigma_e^2), so it strictly compresses the DKKM advantage, and the proposal is right to refuse it. But the constructive half fails on the mechanism test. The claimed DKKM-only object is lambda(h_i)*bm_i, a product of an observable reliability variable and a signal, and the argument is 'FM applies one coefficient per characteristic so it cannot form a product'. That is only true holding the characteristic set fixed -- and P3, from the same proposal set, is simultaneously arguing for engineering 35 characteristics. With one staleness variable and six base chars there are exactly six candidate products; handing FM the six columns h*bm, h*roe, h*agr, h*mom, h*size, h*mkt_lev costs six regressors on 360 months and closes the entire mechanism. The DKKM claim would have to be 'you do not know which products matter', which requires the interaction space to be large, i.e. it is a DIMENSION argument, not a nonlinearity argument -- and at L=6 plus staleness the interaction space is trivially enumerable. Second, the magnitude is bp-level. Take the most favourable case P6 itself constructs, GS21 with rho_z = 0.9655: h uniform on 6-17 gives attenuation from rho^6 = 0.810 to rho^17 = 0.552, so lambda has mean ~0.68 and sd ~0.075, i.e. 11% of its mean. Decompose lambda(h)*bm = E[lambda]*bm + (lambda - E[lambda])*bm; FM takes the first term exactly and, given the h*bm column, the second as well; without the column, the unspanned residual has cross-sectional sd equal to 11% of the bm signal. If the entire bm signal is worth 0.15 of monthly Sharpe -- generous, given GS21's p10-p90 value premium and its 3.9-5.6 bp cross-sectional sd of expected returns -- the unspanned piece is at most 0.11*0.15 = 0.017/month, about 6% of GS21's max_sr of 0.44 and well inside the noise of a 360-month evaluation. In BGN it is smaller still: book = I*num is a small integer averaging 5.95 that changes only when a project is created or dies, so a 12-month-stale bm is nearly identical to a fresh one, and P6 concedes this. Third, and worst for the goal, staleness h_i is by construction uniform and independent of every state variable. It is therefore a pure nuisance coordinate. Injected into the RFF map it enters all 3600 features MULTIPLICATIVELY through sin(gamma*g'x) with a nonzero component on h, degrading every feature; injected into FM it is one additive column. The audit already measured this asymmetry for agr, where a degenerate column raised the PCs needed for 99% of feature variance from 59 to 95. P6 hands DKKM a noise dimension and FM a clean regressor.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM CAN capture it with six interaction columns, which is a smaller code change than P6 itself. FF partially can: P6 concedes the 2x3 design already contains a size interaction, and its escape -- use staleness rather than size as the reliability proxy -- immediately kills the heteroskedastic-noise half of the proposal, which is calibrated on SIZE (sigma_e,i = sigma_e0*(mve_i/median)^{-xi}). The two halves of P6 are therefore in direct tension: the half FF cannot reach (staleness) is worth ~1.7 bp of monthly Sharpe, and the half with real dispersion (size-linked reliability, a 3x noise spread) is exactly the direction FF's double sort already spans. THE ARITHMETIC: at most 0.017 monthly Sharpe in the best model, less than 0.005 in BGN, and zero once FM is given the interactions -- against a target gap of 3-5x. ADDS NOISE FASTER THAN SIGNAL: yes, unambiguously, via the multiplicative nuisance coordinate. METRIC: the population conditional Sharpe would in principle detect a real interaction, but at 1.7 bp/month it is far below the cross-month sampling variation already documented in the correlations table.
verdicts.salvage: Two fragments are worth keeping, neither as a source of a DKKM gap. (1) Breaking the GS21 identity bm = 1/P_ex exactly is worth doing on its own terms -- that identity is the single most indefensible feature of that panel and any referee will find it -- so apply the fiscal-year lag to GS21's accounting chars purely as a realism fix and do not claim a complexity gain. (2) Write up the Fourier argument (classical EIV attenuates the nonlinear span exponentially while attenuating the linear span only by the classical factor) as a short theoretical note in the paper. It is a genuine, non-obvious contribution and it explains why real-data DKKM works DESPITE measurement error rather than because of it -- which is a useful piece of intellectual honesty given that P6's own logic implies real-world EIV should be shrinking the published 3-5x gap, not creating it. Do not implement heteroskedastic noise: it is calibrated on size, which is the one interaction FF already has.

missed_ideas: THE BIGGEST OMISSION: nobody proposed raising the NUMBER OF PRICED AGGREGATE SHOCKS, even though the diagnosis ranked it as lever #2 and DKKM's Theorem 3 makes the effective rank of E[FF'] the literal criterion. All six proposals leave K at 1 (GS21) or 2 (BGN, KP14). With K=1-2 and N=1000, the audit measured that ANY well-diversified portfolio attains SR* to within 0.19%, so every span argument is vacuous before it starts. The defensible implementation is Ross-style APT: replace the single TFP shock with J = 20-40 sectoral/vintage/intangible-capital shocks, each priced, with firm loadings that are NONLINEAR and INTERACTIVE functions of characteristics (e.g. loading on shock j is a bump function of a firm's position in a two-dimensional (size, age) space). Crucially the loadings must be nonlinear in the chars: if B(x) is linear, FM spans D^{-1}B lambda's leading term and we are back to square one. This is the only change that raises EffRank(E[FF']) from single digits into the hundreds through ECONOMICS rather than through feature engineering, and it does not require any 'mispricing' framing.

NOBODY PROPOSED A FALSIFICATION HARNESS BEFORE SPENDING WEEKS ON MODEL CHANGES. The cheapest decisive experiment: bypass the structural models entirely and inject a known nonlinear alpha directly into rp and the corresponding diagonal into cond_var in a synthetic *_moments.pkl, with chars drawn to match a target intrinsic dimension, then run the ACTUAL pipeline (generate_dkkm_factors -> estimate_sdf_dkkm -> evaluate_sdfs -> create_slides_tables) end to end. If the pipeline cannot recover a gap you planted by hand, no economics will help and the estimator is the problem. This costs a day and would have made P2 either mandatory or irrelevant before any of P1/P3/P4/P6 were designed.

NOBODY PROPOSED RUNNING THIS EXACT PIPELINE ON REAL CRSP/COMPUSTAT DATA to verify it reproduces DKKM's published 3-5x. The pipeline has several non-standard elements relative to the published method (a second rank-standardization of the features at dkkm_functions.py:110, NMAT=5 weight averaging, an unpenalized market column, population-conditional-Sharpe evaluation rather than realized OOS tangency Sharpe). If the pipeline does not reproduce the published result on the data where the result is known to hold, every conclusion about the models is confounded. This is the single most informative experiment available and it is absent from all six proposals.

N = 1000 IS A FREE LEVER NOBODY PULLED. The AIPT near-arbitrage term is alpha'D^{-1}alpha ~ N * E[alpha^2/d], so it scales LINEARLY in N; real CRSP has 4000-6000 names. Raising N from 1000 to 5000 multiplies any unspanned premium's contribution to SR*^2 by 5 with zero new economics and zero new parameters, and it also moves the estimator into the P/N regime where the RFF Monte-Carlo error over the kernel is the binding constraint rather than the DGP. It costs O(N^2) in sdf_compute, which is the real reason it was not proposed -- but that trade-off should be stated and priced, not ignored.

NOBODY PROPOSED FIRM ENTRY, EXIT AND AN UNBALANCED PANEL. All three models run a fixed set of 1000 firms with full histories. Real cross-sections have turnover, short histories, and characteristics that are missing or stale for young firms -- which is a major reason real-data DKKM benefits from shrinkage across many weak signals (many firms contribute little information individually). A balanced 1000 x 720 panel with no missingness is the regime in which a correctly specified small model is efficient.

NOBODY PROPOSED MAKING THE TRUE WEIGHT DEPEND ON A THRESHOLD OR REGIME rather than a smooth function. Every nonlinearity in P1/P4/P6 is smooth (a ratio, a power law, a product), and smooth low-order functions of 2-3 chars are exactly what a 21-term quadratic captures -- which is why the proposers' own est3.py has QUAD(21) beating RFF(3600) in the linear-alpha-plus-het-d cell. Genuine kinks are what a Fourier basis reaches and a polynomial does not: financial-constraint regimes, a live default boundary (GS21's is empty), collateral constraints that bind for a state-dependent subset, or option-like payoffs that switch on at a characteristic threshold. P4 makes GS21's default region live as a side effect of raising sigma_z; nobody proposed making a live default/constraint boundary the OBJECTIVE, with the boundary depending on two or three characteristics jointly so that it is a curved surface in char space.

NOBODY ADDRESSED THAT THE EVALUATION METRIC DELETES THE ENTIRE CONDITIONAL-TIMING CHANNEL, and then nobody proposed adding a conditioning mechanism anyway. P5 correctly notes that mean_t(w'rp / sqrt(w'Sigma w)) is homogeneous of degree zero in w, so correct levering-up in high-Sharpe months earns nothing; but no proposal adds time-varying prices of risk interacted with characteristics, which is one of the two channels through which complexity pays in DKKM/KMZ. These have to be fixed TOGETHER: adding char x macro-state interactions to the DGP is pointless while the metric cannot see timing, and fixing the metric is pointless while the DGP has no timing content. Note also that a date-level macro variable is invisible to every cross-sectional weighting scheme (which is why BGN's rf_stand is measurably worthless), so the conditioning must enter as a cross-sectionally varying char x state product.

NOBODY PROPOSED THE QUADRATIC-OLS BENCHMARK AS A STANDING COLUMN. Given that FM plus 15 cross-products beat RFF(3600) in the proposers' own Monte Carlo under the most favourable DGP they tested, a paper claiming 'the virtue of complexity' must report FM-with-interactions in every table. Without it, any measured DKKM-over-FM gap is uninterpretable: it could be complexity, or it could be one interaction layer. This single column would have reframed P1 and P4 before they were written.

NOBODY PROPOSED HETEROGENEITY IN THE LATENT FIRM STATE ITSELF. All the char-engineering proposals expand the MEASUREMENT of a 2-3 dimensional state. The cheaper and more defensible move is to raise the dimension of the state: in BGN, give each firm a firm-specific project-beta distribution (a scale and a shape, not just a common beta_star/scale of 0.772/0.137), so the third sufficient statistic betabar is no longer 99% recoverable from (num, S/num) and the cross-section has 4-5 genuine degrees of freedom instead of 2. In KP14, let lambda_f and the H/L regime be firm-specific and persistent. This changes the DGP's intrinsic dimension, which is the quantity that actually drives the feature spectrum, and unlike P3 it cannot be dismissed as relabelling.

NOBODY CHECKED THE FF/FM MARKET-COLUMN ASYMMETRY. fama_functions.fama_french sets the last column to the VALUE-weighted market (mve/mve.sum()) while fama_macbeth sets it to the EQUAL-weighted market (1/len(d)), and dkkm's mve_data always appends the value-weighted market UNPENALIZED (dkkm_functions.py:289-290, 309 excludes the last column from the augmentation). Since the audit shows the alpha->infinity limit of DKKM is exactly the CAPM, and since in GS21 89-97% of max SR^2 comes from the alpha leg rather than the market leg, this asymmetry is doing real work in the reported comparisons and is never disclosed.
